To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the PPIase activity of Cpr7, a CyP-40 family cyclophilin, is not essential for rapid growth or Hsp70-dependent steroid receptor activation, and (2) the TPR-containing C terminus is sufficient for Cpr7 function in vivo.

a functional assessment of a cyclophilin PPIase domain was performed in vivo by using a mutant of the S. cerevisiae Cy-P40 homolog, and that the PPIase was found to be dispensable for growth or steroid receptor activity.
the peptidyl prolyl isomeras (PPIase), or rotamase, domain of the CyP40 cyclophilin homolog Cpr7 is not required to support growth or glucocorticoid receptor activity in Saccharomyce cerevisiae.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a family of molecular chaperones that function to stabilize steroid hormone receptors.
the role of Cpr7 in the regulation of the glucocorticoid receptor in the yeast Saccharomyces Cerevisiae.
the function of cyclophilins in eukaryotic cells, particularly in relation to the molecular chaperone activity of the Hsp90·Steroid receptor complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PPIase activity of Cpr7 does not contribute to the growth and steroid receptor activity of the yeast.
the Cpr7 PPIase domain does not play a role in the growth of yeast or the glucocorticoid receptor activity of yeast.
the PPIase catalytic activity of CyP-40 proteins is not required for their essential function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cpr7 is an important component of the steroid receptor chaperone machinery, but the PPIase activity of the protein is not required to support this activity.
the Cpr7 PPIase domain is not required for Cpr7 function, and therefore, it is not likely to be a direct participant in Hsp90·receptor complex assembly or activity.
the PPIase activity of Cpr7, and perhaps CyP-40 in general, is not essential to maintain Hsp90 function in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PPIase domains of the CyP40s are not required for growth or glucocorticoid receptor activity in vivo.
the PPIase activity is not essential for Cpr7 function, but the PPIase is not a superfluous appendage to the Cpr7 protein.
the PPIase domains of Cpr7 and CyP-40 do not contribute significantly to Cpr7-dependent growth or glucocorticoid receptor activity.
